description: Constituent Assembly + landmark dates across tiers

questions.stem: The Constitution of India was ADOPTED on:
questions.explanation: Constitution was ADOPTED on 26 Nov 1949 (hence celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas from 2015). It came into FORCE on 26 January 1950 — Republic Day.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution was:
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee (Aug 1947 onwards). Rajendra Prasad was PRESIDENT of the Constituent Assembly. Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution (Dec 1946).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Constituent Assembly took approximately how long to frame the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Famously 2 years, 11 months and 18 days (9 Dec 1946 first sitting → 26 Nov 1949 adoption). 11 sessions, 165 days of sitting. 165 amendments made; the final document had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules at the time of adoption.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Match the FEATURE of the Indian Constitution with its SOURCE. A. Parliamentary system. B. Fundamental Rights. C. Directive Principles. D. Emergency provisions (suspension of FRs). List-II: 1. USA. 2. Ireland. 3. UK. 4. Weimar Germany.
questions.explanation: Parliamentary govt → UK. Fundamental Rights → USA (Bill of Rights). DPSPs → Ireland. Emergency + suspension of FRs during Emergency → Weimar Constitution of Germany (1919). Other borrowings: Federal structure + residuary powers → Canada; Concurrent List → Australia; Judicial review → USA.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Preamble's words 'Socialist, Secular and Integrity' were added by which amendment?
questions.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) — 'Mini-Constitution' — added 'Socialist, Secular, and Integrity' to the Preamble, plus Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A), and extended LS terms. 44th Amendment (1978) reversed some of the 42nd's emergency-era excesses.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES. 1. They were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. 2. They are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution. 3. There were originally 10 Fundamental Duties; the 11th (education of a child/ward aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment. 4. Fundamental Duties are justiciable and can be enforced through courts. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — Fundamental Duties are NON-JUSTICIABLE (like DPSPs). They cannot be enforced by writs. They are, however, moral obligations for citizens. Parliament can enact laws for non-compliance (e.g. Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971). Other three statements are correct.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): The Indian Constitution is described as 'federal in form but unitary in spirit'. REASON (R): Under Article 356, the Centre can impose President's Rule in a state, centralising powers.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: K. C. Wheare called India 'quasi-federal'. Federal features: 3-list division of powers (Union, State, Concurrent), independent judiciary, bicameral Parliament. UNITARY tilts: single citizenship, strong Centre (all-India services), Art 356 (President's Rule), Art 249 (Parliament can legislate on state list if RS so resolves), single integrated judiciary. Art 356 is the single strongest centralising lever — correctly given as the reason.
